title: The filters: theory and computation
text: series \(\vx = (x_1, \dots, x_T)^\top\) \((T - 2) \times T\) matrix \(\mK\) second differences (rows \((1, -2, 1)\)), trend minimises \(\lVert\vx - \vg\rVert^2 + \lambda\lVert\mK\vg\rVert^2\), \[ \hat{\vg} = (\mI + \lambda\mA)^{-1}\vx = \mB\vx, \qquad \mA = \mK^\top\mK , \] \(\hat{\vc} = \vx - \hat{\vg}\). \(\mK\vone = \mathbf{0}\), every row \(\mB\) sums one: trend weighted average observations. Computation. \(\mI + \lambda\mA\) symmetric, positive definite pentadiagonal. package factors \(\mL\mD\mL^\top\) unit lower-triangular \(\mL\) bandwidth two solves \(O(T)\) operations; version 0.1.0 solved dense \(T \times T\) system, \(O(T^3)\), every \(\lambda\) search.

title: The filters: theory and computation
text: McDermott (1997) chooses \(\lambda\) cross-validation: leave one observation, predict trend others, sum squared errors. Generalised cross-validation (Craven Wahba 1979) replaces leave-one-errors \[ \mathrm{GCV}(\lambda) = \frac{T^{-1}\sum_t\left(x_t - \hat{g}_t(\lambda)\right)^2}{\left(1 - T^{-1}\tr\mB(\lambda)\right)^2} \] (Choudhary et al. 2014, eq. 5), papers code use approximation \[ \mathrm{GCV}(\lambda) \approx \frac{1}{T}\left(1 + \frac{2T}{\lambda}\right)\sum_t\left(x_t - \hat{g}_t(\lambda)\right)^2 \] (eq. 6, attributed Silverman 1984). mhp_filter() minimises approximation \(\lambda = 1, \dots,\) max_lambda default, exact criterion criterion = "exact": eigenvalues \(\mu_i\) \(\mA\), computed , give \(\tr\mB(\lambda) = \sum_i (1 + \lambda\mu_i)^{-1}\) residual sum squares every \(\lambda\) \(O(T)\) operations.  exact criterion falls steadily \(\lambda\) falls, \(\lambda = 1\), trend almost interpolates series: generalised cross-validation known undersmooth series whose deviations trend autocorrelated, business cycles . approximation adds much heavier penalty small \(\lambda\) (\(\lambda = 683\) factor \(1 + 2T/\lambda\) 1.59, 1.17 exact one), penalty, cross-validation , gives modified HP filter interior minimum. package keeps published approximation default.

text: mhpfilter splits macroeconomic time series trend cycle Hodrick-Prescott (HP) filter two versions whose settings come data: hp_filter(): HP filter fixed smoothing parameter (1600 quarterly, 100 annual); mhp_filter(): modified HP filter McDermott (1997), assessed Choudhary, Hanif Iqbal (2014): every series gets smoothing parameter minimises generalised cross-validation criterion (published approximation, exact criterion); fmhp_filter(): fully modified HP filter Hanif, Iqbal Choudhary (2017), also reduces end-point bias HP filter raising smoothing parameter first last observations, linear quadratic weights chosen minimise end-point loss Bloechl (2014). Version 1.0.0 keeps every function, argument result version 0.1.0 adds fully modified HP filter. title: Modified Hodrick-Prescott filter: the smoothing parameter chosen from the data — mhp_filter
text: candidate \(\lambda\) trend \(\hat{\mathbf{g}}(\lambda)\) hp_filter() computed $$\mathrm{GCV}(\lambda) = \frac{1}{T}\left(1 + \frac{2T}{\lambda}\right)\sum_{t=1}^{T}\left(x_t -   \hat{g}_t(\lambda)\right)^2$$ (Choudhary et al. 2014, eq. 6; Hanif et al. 2017, eq. 4); \(\hat\lambda\) minimises . Silverman's (1984) approximation generalised cross-validation (Craven Wahba 1979), $$\mathrm{GCV}(\lambda) = \frac{T^{-1}\sum_{t}(x_t - \hat{g}_t(\lambda))^2}{\left(1 -   T^{-1}\mathrm{tr}\,\mathbf{B}(\lambda)\right)^2}$$ (Choudhary et al. 2014, eq. 5), criterion = "exact" uses: eigenvalues \(\mu_i\) \(\mathbf{}\), computed , give \(\mathrm{tr}\,\mathbf{B}(\lambda) = \sum_i (1 + \lambda\mu_i)^{-1}\) residual sum squares every \(\lambda\) \(O(T)\) operations (decomposition costs \(O(T^3)\), fraction second hundred observations). trend costs \(O(T)\) operations, search 100000 values takes second 200 quarterly observations. search authors' MATLAB code (modifiedhpfilternew.m, Choudhary et al. 2014), omits factor \(1/T\) (change minimum) works series given; filter logarithm series (papers) log_scale = TRUE passing log(x). Changes version 0.1.0. criterion unchanged (help page 0.1.0 printed factor \(1 + 2/(T\lambda)\), code used \(1 + 2T/\lambda\)); every trend now banded solve instead dense one, results agree 0.1.0 rounding error fraction time.
